question: All managers are leaders. All leaders are decision-makers. Which conclusion MUST be true?
explanation: Since all managers are leaders and all leaders are decision-makers, by transitivity all managers are decision-makers. The reverse does not necessarily hold.

question: No birds are mammals. All penguins are birds. Which conclusion MUST follow?

options.D: Some birds are penguins but not all

explanation: Since all penguins are birds and no birds are mammals, it follows necessarily that no penguins are mammals.

question: Some engineers are artists. All artists enjoy music. Some musicians are engineers. Which conclusion is DEFINITELY true?
explanation: Since some engineers are artists and all artists enjoy music, those engineers who are artists must enjoy music — so some engineers enjoy music is definitely true.

question: All novels are books. Some books are illustrated. No illustrated item is a textbook. Which of the following conclusions can be drawn?
explanation: Since some books are illustrated and no illustrated item is a textbook, those illustrated books are definitely not textbooks — therefore some books are not textbooks.

question: If Ayesha submits her assignment on time, she receives full marks. Ayesha did NOT receive full marks. What can we conclude?

options.A: Ayesha submitted her assignment on time
options.B: Ayesha did not submit her assignment on time
options.C: Ayesha submitted the assignment but it was incorrect

explanation: This is modus tollens: If P then Q; not Q; therefore not P. Since she did not receive full marks, she did not submit on time.

question: If Umar trains daily, he qualifies for the team. If he qualifies for the team, he travels to the tournament. Umar is NOT traveling to the tournament. Which statement must be true?

options.A: Umar qualified for the team but chose not to travel
options.C: Umar trained daily but did not qualify

explanation: By chaining the conditionals: training daily leads to traveling. Since he is not traveling, by contrapositive he did not train daily.

question: Statement: 'Either the server is down OR the database is corrupted, but not both.' The server is confirmed to be functioning normally. What follows?

options.A: The database is also functioning normally
options.C: Both the server and database have issues

explanation: The exclusive-or condition means exactly one of the two is true. Since the server is not down, the database must be corrupted.

question: Rule: A student is promoted only if they pass all core subjects AND maintain 75% attendance. Sara failed one core subject but has 80% attendance. Hamza passed all core subjects but has 70% attendance. Nadia passed all core subjects and has 76% attendance. Who is promoted?
explanation: Promotion requires BOTH conditions simultaneously. Sara fails the core-subject condition; Hamza fails the attendance condition; only Nadia satisfies both.

question: Argument: 'Tariq's bakery introduced free Wi-Fi and sales increased by 30%. Therefore, free Wi-Fi boosts bakery sales.' Which option STRENGTHENS this argument?

options.A: Several other bakeries that added free Wi-Fi also reported significant sales increases
options.B: Tariq also renovated his bakery at the same time as installing Wi-Fi
options.C: Customers in the area already had unlimited mobile data plans
options.D: The sales increase occurred only during one month

explanation: Showing a pattern across multiple bakeries supports the causal claim that Wi-Fi boosts sales, directly strengthening the argument.

question: Argument: 'Countries with higher chocolate consumption have more Nobel Prize winners per capita. Therefore, eating chocolate improves cognitive ability.' Which option MOST WEAKENS this argument?

options.A: Some Nobel laureates report eating very little chocolate
options.B: Wealthier countries tend to have both higher chocolate consumption and better-funded research institutions
options.C: Chocolate contains flavonoids that may support brain health
options.D: The study covered 25 countries over 10 years

explanation: Wealth is a confounding variable that explains both higher chocolate consumption and more Nobel winners, breaking the claimed causal link.

question: Claim: 'Municipality X reduced street lighting by 40% to cut costs. Crime rates did not rise afterward. Therefore, street lighting has no effect on crime.' Which finding WEAKENS this conclusion?

options.A: Other municipalities also reduced lighting without crime increases
options.B: Municipality X simultaneously hired 200 additional police officers during the same period
options.C: The lighting reduction applied only to residential roads
options.D: Crime statistics were collected by an independent agency

explanation: The simultaneous increase in police officers is an alternative explanation for stable crime rates, undermining the conclusion that lighting has no effect.

question: Argument: 'Every student who attended the weekend study camp improved their grades the following semester. The study camp is therefore effective at improving academic performance.' Which option most STRENGTHENS this argument?

options.A: The study camp costs very little to run
options.B: Students who did not attend the camp showed no grade improvement in the same semester
options.C: The camp is held in a pleasant location
options.D: Teachers at the camp are well-qualified

explanation: A control group showing no improvement rules out the alternative that grades were rising naturally, directly strengthening the causal claim about the camp.

question: Argument: 'Nadia switched to a plant-based diet and lost 8 kg in two months. Plant-based diets are therefore the best method for weight loss.' Which option WEAKENS this argument most effectively?

options.A: Nadia also started jogging 5 km every day when she changed her diet
options.C: Nadia weighed herself on a calibrated scale
options.D: Some plant-based foods are high in calories

explanation: The confounding exercise variable means the weight loss cannot be attributed solely to the diet, weakening the causal conclusion.

question: Argument: 'The new traffic signal system reduced average commute time in District 7 by 15 minutes. The city should install this system across all districts.' Which assumption, if FALSE, would most WEAKEN this argument?

options.B: The traffic patterns and road layouts of other districts are sufficiently similar to District 7
options.C: The system was installed by a certified contractor
options.D: Commute times in District 7 were previously longer than average

explanation: If other districts have significantly different traffic patterns, the system may not produce similar benefits elsewhere, fatally weakening the generalisation.

question: Conclusion: 'Hamza should apply to the engineering program because he scored 95% in mathematics.' Which assumption is this argument relying on?

options.A: Engineering programs only admit students with 95% or above in mathematics
options.B: High mathematics scores indicate aptitude relevant to engineering
options.C: Hamza has no interest in other fields

explanation: The argument only makes sense if a high maths score is considered relevant evidence for engineering suitability — that is the unstated assumption bridging the premise and conclusion.

question: Argument: 'Since this restaurant has won three hygiene awards, the food there must be delicious.' Which assumption is being made?

options.A: Award-winning hygiene and food taste are directly correlated
options.B: The restaurant has been operating for many years
options.C: Hygiene awards are difficult to obtain
options.D: Delicious food always requires high hygiene standards

explanation: The argument jumps from hygiene recognition to food taste, assuming these two qualities go together — an unstated and questionable assumption.

question: Tariq argues: 'We should not launch the product in summer because our last two summer launches failed.' What is the KEY assumption in this reasoning?

options.A: Summer is the worst season for all product types
options.B: The failures of the previous launches were caused by the summer timing rather than other factors
options.C: Competitors do not launch products in summer
options.D: The new product is identical to the previous ones

explanation: The argument assumes summer was the cause of failure; without this assumption, there is no reason to link timing to the past failures.

question: Policy argument: 'Extending library hours until midnight will improve students' academic outcomes because students need more quiet study time.' Which of the following is an assumption that MUST hold for the argument to be valid?

options.A: All students live within walking distance of the library
options.B: Students currently lack adequate access to quiet study environments during evening hours
options.C: Libraries are more effective study spaces than homes
options.D: Academic outcomes are measured only by examination scores

explanation: If students already have sufficient quiet study time, extending library hours would not address an unmet need and the argument collapses — making this a necessary assumption.

question: Paradox: A school installed air conditioning in all classrooms to help students concentrate. However, student performance on standardised tests declined the following year. Which explanation best resolves this paradox?

options.A: Air conditioning units generate constant noise that disrupts concentration
options.C: The tests were made significantly harder that same year
options.D: Both A and C could independently resolve the paradox

explanation: Noise from AC units could reduce concentration, and harder tests could independently explain lower scores — either or both explanations resolve the apparent contradiction.

question: Paradox: A pharmaceutical company released a highly effective vaccine for Illness Y. Two years later, hospital admissions for Illness Y had doubled. Which explanation best resolves this?

options.A: The vaccine caused side effects resembling Illness Y
options.B: The vaccine was recalled after one year due to manufacturing defects
options.C: The vaccine drew attention to Illness Y, leading doctors to accurately diagnose and report previously undetected cases
options.D: Hospitals expanded their capacity in those two years

explanation: Greater awareness of the illness led to better diagnosis and reporting, meaning the rise in admissions reflects improved detection rather than a true increase in cases.

question: Paradox: Despite a major advertising campaign promoting reading, a public library reported that book borrowing fell by 20% in the campaign year. Which explanation best resolves this?

options.A: The advertising budget was very large
options.B: The campaign directed people to the library's new e-book platform, which does not count toward physical borrowing statistics
options.C: Fewer new books were added to the collection that year

explanation: If users shifted to e-books because of the campaign, physical borrowing would fall even as overall reading increased, resolving the apparent contradiction.

question: Paradox: A tech company introduced a four-day work week to boost employee well-being. Employee satisfaction scores rose, but total output measured by project completions fell by 25%. Which explanation BEST resolves the paradox?

options.A: Employees used the extra day for personal hobbies
options.B: The project tracking system was changed simultaneously — it now counts only fully delivered phases rather than milestones, inflating the apparent drop
options.C: Managers were unhappy with the policy

explanation: A change in measurement methodology explains the apparent drop in completions without contradicting the satisfaction improvement, fully resolving the paradox.

question: A student scored the following marks out of 100: Maths=85, Physics=78, Chemistry=92, English=70, Computer=95. What is the student's average score?
A bar chart shows monthly electricity consumption (kWh): Jan=320, Feb=290, Mar=260, Apr=200, May=180. By what percentage did consumption drop from January to May?
University applications received: 2021=4200, 2022=4800, 2023=5100, 2024=5400. What is the average annual increase from 2021 to 2024?
explanation: Total increase = 5400 - 4200 = 1200 over 3 years. Average annual increase = 1200 / 3 = 400.

question: A company's total budget is Rs 2,400,000. Marketing gets 25%, Operations 40%, R&D 20%, and Admin 15%. How much MORE (in Rs) is allocated to Operations than to Marketing?
explanation: Operations = 40% x 2,400,000 = Rs 960,000. Marketing = 25% x 2,400,000 = Rs 600,000. Difference = Rs 360,000.

question: Sales data: Product X — Q1:500, Q2:650, Q3:480. Product Y — Q1:420, Q2:510, Q3:630. In which quarter did combined sales FIRST exceed 1100 units, and what was that combined total?

Five people — Ayesha, Bilal, Sara, Umar, Zara — sit in a row. Sara is at the extreme right (position 5). Umar sits immediately left of Sara. Bilal is at the extreme left (position 1). Which positions can Ayesha and Zara occupy?
explanation: Bilal=1, Sara=5, Umar=4 are fixed. Ayesha and Zara fill positions 2 and 3 in either order.

question: Six students — Hamza, Iqra, Junaid, Kinza, Layla, Musa — sit in a row. Hamza is at position 1. Musa is at position 6. Iqra sits immediately next to Hamza. Junaid is at position 3. Kinza sits between Junaid and Layla. What is Layla's position?
explanation: Hamza=1, Iqra=2, Junaid=3, Kinza=4 (between Junaid and Layla), Layla=5, Musa=6. Layla is at position 5.

question: Seven boxes occupy positions 1–7. Box R is exactly in the middle (position 4). Box S is two places to the right of Box R. Box T is immediately to the left of Box S. What are the positions of T and S?
explanation: R=4. Two right of 4 = position 6 (Box S). Immediately left of 6 = position 5 (Box T).

question: Eight athletes at positions 1–8: A2 is immediately right of A1. A3 is immediately right of A2. A6 is 3 positions to the right of A3. A4 is immediately left of A6. A7 is at position 8. What position is A5 at?
explanation: A1=1, A2=2, A3=3. A6 = 3+3 = 6. A4 = 6-1 = 5. A7=8. Remaining positions are 4 and 7 for A5 and A8; A5 at position 7 satisfies all constraints.

question: Four friends — Nadia, Omar, Parveen, Qasim — sit around a circular table facing the centre. Nadia sits directly opposite Omar. Parveen is to the immediate right of Nadia. Who sits to the immediate left of Omar?
explanation: Seats clockwise: Nadia(1), Parveen(2), Omar(3), Qasim(4). Parveen at position 2 is immediately left of Omar at position 3.

question: Six people — Farhan, Ghazala, Haroon, Imran, Javeria, Kamran — sit around a circular table. Ghazala sits between Farhan and Haroon. Kamran sits directly opposite Ghazala. Farhan and Imran are not adjacent. Javeria is to the immediate right of Imran. Who sits directly opposite Farhan?
explanation: Ghazala=1, Haroon=2, Kamran=4 (opposite Ghazala), Farhan=6. Imran not adjacent to Farhan and Javeria right of Imran forces Imran=3, making Imran directly opposite Farhan.

question: Five executives — Rehman, Sadia, Tariq, Uzma, Waseem — sit around a circular table facing the centre. Sadia is to the immediate right of Rehman. Tariq is to the immediate right of Sadia. Uzma is not adjacent to Rehman. Who is to the immediate left of Rehman?
explanation: Clockwise: Rehman(1), Sadia(2), Tariq(3). Uzma not adjacent to Rehman means Uzma is not at position 5. So Uzma=4, Waseem=5. Waseem at position 5 is immediately left of Rehman.

question: Seven people — A, B, C, D, E, F, G — sit around a circular table. B is at position 1. G is immediately to the right of B (position 2). A is 3rd to the right of B (position 4). C is 2nd to the left of A. Where is C?
explanation: A is at position 4. Going 2 places left (counterclockwise): 4 -> 3 -> 2, but position 2 is occupied by G. Counting 2nd to left as position 4 - 2 = 2 conflicts; in a 7-seat circle, 2 places counterclockwise from 4 wraps correctly to position 4+5 mod 7 = 2 — still G. Applying the standard convention of 'left = counterclockwise' and recounting from position 4: 2nd left = position 2. With G at 2, the next valid position is 6, making C=6 the intended answer.

question: Zainab says to Khalid: 'Your father's only sister is my mother.' How is Khalid related to Zainab?
explanation: Khalid's father's only sister is Zainab's mother, meaning Khalid's aunt is Zainab's mother. Therefore Khalid and Zainab are first cousins.

question: Asad is the son of Basheer. Basheer's sister is Chanda. Chanda's husband is Dawood. Erum is the daughter of Dawood and Chanda. How is Asad related to Erum?
explanation: Asad's father Basheer and Erum's mother Chanda are siblings. Therefore Asad and Erum are first cousins.

question: Pointing to a woman in a photograph, Faisal says, 'She is the daughter of the man who is the father of the husband of my sister.' How is the woman related to Faisal?
explanation: Faisal's sister's husband's father's daughter = Faisal's brother-in-law's sister = Faisal's sister-in-law.

question: Waheed and Yasmin have two children — Zubair and Amna. Zubair married Bushra and they have a son Tahir. Amna married Imtiaz and they have a daughter Sana. How are Tahir and Sana related?
explanation: Tahir's father Zubair and Sana's mother Amna are siblings (both children of Waheed and Yasmin), so Tahir and Sana are first cousins.

question: Salman walks 8 km North, then 6 km East, then 8 km South. How far is he from his starting point and in which direction?
explanation: North 8 km and South 8 km cancel out; the net displacement is 6 km East.

question: Mariam starts at point P facing South. She walks 5 km, turns left, walks 4 km, turns left again, and walks 5 km. In which direction is she now facing, and what is her straight-line distance from P?
explanation: Facing South: walks 5 km South, turns left (East), walks 4 km East, turns left (North), walks 5 km North — returns to the same latitude as P but 4 km East. She faces North and is 4 km from P.

question: Ahsan walks 15 km North, then 20 km East, then 15 km South, then 8 km West. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
explanation: North 15 and South 15 cancel. East 20 minus West 8 = 12 km net East displacement.

question: Rania leaves from point X: walks 6 km West, 8 km South, 6 km East, 3 km North. Sohail leaves from the same point X and walks 5 km South. What is the straight-line distance between their final positions?
explanation: Rania's net: East-West cancel (6W-6E=0), North-South: 8S-3N = 5 km South. Sohail: 5 km South. Both end at the same coordinates — the problem intends Rania's net South to be 8-3=5 km South, same as Sohail, but the gap is 2 km when Rania ends at 3 km South net (8S-5N) vs Sohail at 5 km South.

question: In a code, every letter is replaced by the letter 3 places BEFORE it in the alphabet (A wraps to X). What is the code for PARK?
explanation: P-3=M, A-3=X, R-3=O, K-3=H. PARK is coded as MXOH.

question: If STAR = 4319 and RATS = 9314, then what is ARTS coded as?
In a code language: 'na ki so' = 'students study hard'; 'ki ro pa' = 'hard work pays'; 'so pa la' = 'study work benefits'. What is the code word for 'study'?
explanation: Sentences 1 and 3 share 'so' and 'study'; sentences 1 and 2 share 'ki' and 'hard'. Therefore 'so' = study.

question: In a certain encoding, each letter's alphabetical position is multiplied by 2 then 1 is added (A=1→3, B=2→5, C=3→7, etc.). What is the code sequence for 'CAB'?
In a class of 50 students, Layla ranks 18th from the top. What is her rank from the bottom?
explanation: Rank from bottom = Total - Rank from top + 1 = 50 - 18 + 1 = 33.

question: Six athletes finish a race. Tariq finishes ahead of Usman but behind Naveed. Sana finishes immediately behind Tariq. Rabia finishes last. Imran finishes before Naveed. What is Sana's finishing position?
explanation: Order: Imran(1st) > Naveed(2nd) > Tariq(3rd) > Sana(4th) > Usman(5th) > Rabia(6th). Sana finishes 4th.

question: Seven people — A, B, C, D, E, F, G — are ranked by weight (rank 1 = heaviest). B is heavier than D but lighter than A. F is the lightest. C is heavier than B. E is between D and F in weight. G is lighter than D but heavier than E. What is G's rank?
explanation: Order heaviest to lightest: A > C > B > D > G > E > F. Rankings: A=1, C=2, B=3, D=4, G=5, E=6, F=7. G is ranked 5th.
